claims.text: The coating consists of alternating nanoscale FCC and BCC high-entropy-alloy layers.
The multilayer exhibits compositional complexity, severe lattice distortion, and short-range order.
Progressive plastic deformation under sustained creep loading is governed by dislocation accumulation at FCC/BCC interfaces.
Dislocation accumulation at the interfaces produces localized shear bands.
Lattice distortion and short-range order impede dislocation motion.
Lattice distortion and short-range order limit slip transfer between FCC and BCC layers.
Dislocations nucleate within the individual HEA layers during sustained loading.
FCC/BCC interfaces impede dislocations because of lattice distortion and compositional complexity.
Once interfacial dislocations reach a critical concentration, plastic deformation localizes into shear bands at the interfaces.
Interfacial shear bands progressively accommodate creep strain.
Creep loading will increase dislocation density relative to a low-stress baseline.
Creep loading will produce preferential shear-band formation at FCC/BCC interfaces.
Creep deformation will be spatially non-uniform and dominated by the interfaces.
The as-deposited or minimally stressed baseline has low dislocation density and lacks significant localized deformation.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the nanoscale multilayer architecture remains intact and before extensive grain-boundary sliding, delamination, or interface decohesion.
The interfacial dislocation density should significantly exceed the dislocation density in the layer interiors under sustained creep loading.
